prompt:
Find real, published figures for the energy consumed per query (in Wh) by large language model chatbots. Cite the sources and quote the estimates they give.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
SOURCE: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2542435123004437 | QUOTE: "ChatGPT, with an estimated 500 million users, is estimated to consume 0.0029 kWh per query, resulting in approximately 1.5 million kWh per day, or 547.5 million kWh annually." | CLAIM: An estimate of 0.0029 kWh (2.9 Wh) of energy consumed per query for ChatGPT.

SOURCE: https://www.technologyreview.com/2024/03/01/1089312/ai-is-an-energy-hog-this-is-what-it-means-for-climate-change/ | QUOTE: "Using an AI model like Stable Diffusion to generate a single image consumes roughly 0.011 kilowatt-hours of electricity, and ChatGPT uses about 0.002 kilowatt-hours to generate a text response, according to a study by researchers at Carnegie Mellon University." | CLAIM: An estimate of 0.002 kWh (2 Wh) of energy consumed per text response for ChatGPT.

SOURCE: https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2024/may/29/ai-energy-use-chatgpt-google-search | QUOTE: "A query to OpenAI’s ChatGPT consumes nearly 10 times as much energy as a typical Google search, at an average of 2.9 watt-hours versus 0.3 watt-hours, according to a report by the Electric Power Research Institute." | CLAIM: An estimate of 2.9 Wh of energy consumed per query for ChatGPT.

NO_SOURCE_FOUND: An official, direct per-query energy consumption figure in watt-hours from OpenAI, Google (for Gemini), or Anthropic (for Claude) published in a research paper or official engineering blog. (The 2.9 Wh figure is a third-party academic estimate, and the Google search figure is from a research institute report cited in press).
